name: Matic
description: A robot vacuum/mop that navigates with 5 RGB-infrared cameras and an on-device NVIDIA Jetson Orin running long-term SLAM instead of LiDAR — all mapping and cleaning data stays on the robot and inside the home network. Sold direct-only with a 6-month return window; the dock is charging-only, with no auto-empty, mop-wash, or water-refill.

sourcing: Specs sourced from Matic's own product and FAQ pages (maticrobots.com/product, support.maticrobots.com/frequently-asked-questions), Vacuum Wars' hands-on review, and RobotVacHub's review, as of September 2026. Price was checked directly against maticrobots.com/product on the date this page was written and against independent reporting of the change: Matic raised its base price from $1,245 to $1,495 effective September 9, 2026 due to rising component costs — this is a price increase, not a discount lapsing, and some review coverage published before the change date still shows the superseded $1,245 figure. Robot weight is not published by Matic and was not found in either review checked. Water-tank coverage area is given inconsistently across sources (~800 sq ft on Matic's own page vs. ~1,300 sq ft per the FAQ) and is noted here rather than resolved in one direction. robotindex does not sell this product.

pricing.summary: Base configuration (one robot, one dock) is **$1,495** as of this writing. Matic raised its price from $1,245 to $1,495 effective **September 9, 2026**, citing rising costs for memory and other components — a genuine increase, not a temporary discount lapsing, and several secondary write-ups published just before or around the change date still show the old $1,245 figure. Multi-dock and two-robot bundles run from $1,593 up to $2,990.

editorial.heading: Privacy & Navigation
editorial.body: Where most flagship robot vacuums use LiDAR turrets, Matic navigates entirely on cameras: 5 RGB-infrared cameras feeding an onboard NVIDIA Jetson Orin that runs long-term SLAM mapping and recognizes people, pets, and kids for collision avoidance. Matic states that audio and video data "never leaves your home" — processing is on-device, and any network communication stays inside the home network rather than a vendor cloud. This local-only approach is the main reason the product fits this site's focus, though independent reviews note the tradeoff: navigation runs noticeably slower than LiDAR-based competitors (RobotVacHub measured 227 minutes for a run other flagships complete in roughly 60).

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: The dock is charging-only — no auto-empty, no mop-washing, no water-refill — which independent reviewers describe as the single most-cited complaint given the flagship price point. Matic previously sold a $125/month rental subscription starting in 2023 before discontinuing it in favor of the current purchase-only model with a 6-month return window. Robot weight is not published by Matic and wasn't found in either review checked.

firmwareCommunity.note: Matic has not released a public SDK, firmware repo, or developer API. Not currently listed in Builds & Mods.
